Amazing interview with Linus Torvalds at TED

I often thought that the TED organizer (interviewer) looked like a prick but I feel bad about it now - he was smart about his questions and very tactful with Linus despite how bad such an interview could be handled. I mean, I've seen people interviewing presidents and cutting them off, this guy really treats Linus with the full respect he deserves and it lead to a not perfect, but great interview!
I wouldn't say amazing interview, but still interesting

It's pretty amazing that he is doing a TED talk, and he is actually being interviewed in an official TED event, not even a TEDx (independent TED). Have you ever seen an interview being conducted at TED? I guess not, because they are named TED talks not TED interviews...

Sure the interview could be better as I said in my other comment here but just the fact it exists is amazing, plus it has plenty of very good moments for something that is not even half an hour long.

I'm sure there are more, but the only other interview I recall seeing at an official TED event was Elon Musk. That puts Linus in good company.

It is a pretty big deal. There are plenty of highly successful people who will go to the trouble of putting together a 20 minute talk to get in front of that audience. The fact that the TED organizers are willing to do all of the preparation to have a guest on their stage says a lot about that guest.

Absolutely agree and I'd like to add that this format could have been chosen because Linus wouldn't feel comfortable addressing an audience by himself. You can see that much of the talk focuses around the point that he is not a people person - so he could either have demanded such a format (which he is used to from Linux conferences, many of which I've seen online) or the TED organizers felt he wouldn't do well in the specific format of an "inspiring TED speech". If you explore the comments you'll even see some people criticizing his communication skills even as an interviewee.

My personal opinion though, is that even if Linus is a huge introvert they really did exaggerate this point to the extent it's just not true. He is a bona-fide genius and orchestrates a thousand people every two months as he says himself. He is not as socially awkward or ignorant as he pretends to be here. He could just be playing along to the interviewer's take on him. I'd go as far as to say he understands people better than the average person - he just refuses to adapt to the common way of thinking and acting, for which I commend him.

He'd do fine in a normal TED talk if he put himself to it but he probably just doesn't want to or thinks he wouldn't have a definite point to make in such a presentation. Anyway, I'm glad they did the interview, the end result was pretty good but it does paint him as a sort of autistic, which he really isn't. Only a fool would think someone with a crushing social deficiency would achieve half of what Linus has achieved. It's almost an insult to people who do have social phobias. He always knows what he is doing and he is doing it with a purpose in mind.

Anyone watching the interview a second time can see that Linus, even if a little anxious is enjoying himself there in front of an audience.

Lessons learned from Linux Mint as a Windows user.

  • Linux Mint 17.3 is the Linux kernel + pre-installed add-ons.
  • There are many different UI variants of the same Mint 17.3: Cinnamon, Mate, KDE and Xfce, that can be regarded as some Windows desktop themes. (Different icons, different order of the buttons, different sound effects, different color, style)
  • In the Cinnamon desktop theme, what you think is "File Explorer" is actually an application called "Nemo".
  • "Nemo" is an improved version of "Nautilus" which still exists and can be found. And this is the cool thing you can run both of them in parallel!
  • Looks and feels almost the same as Windows File explore, even connecting to the network shares are almost the same. You click on it and it asks for a login and password.
  • In the right bottom bar you have an icon that when you click on it, you get a dialog box that searches for updates. It even gives a "!" sign to tell you that there are new updates.

And the most important thing: It does not matter if you choose Cinnamon or KDE or Mate....

Once installed you can convert from cinnamon to KDE and the other way around similar like you would change Windows desktop styles. You don't have to reformat and reinstall everything,
